reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates carbon-induced TWIP/TRIP in a metastable dual-phase HEA, but this is a fundamentally different system from the single-phase BCC refractory alloy in the hypothesis; no evidence is provided that such mechanisms can operate in BCC refractory HEAs or that carbon preserves strength in this context. The claim about avoiding carbide precipitation at 0.3–0.5 at.% C is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Interstitial carbon can activate TWIP/TRIP mechanisms in high-entropy alloys
TWIP/TRIP mechanisms enhance plasticity by increasing strain hardening and ductility
Carbon addition provides solid solution strengthening to preserve high yield strength
The cited TWIP/TRIP effects are achievable in a refractory BCC HEA like NbZrTiHfMo
A low carbon concentration (0.3–0.5 at.%) avoids carbide precipitation that would degrade ductility
